title: FreeRDP shadow server accepts unauthenticated Fast-Path input before session activation
summary: Before a shadow server reaches the authenticated active-session state, its Fast-Path input handlers forward mouse, keyboard and synchronization events to the X11 backend without the state guard used by the slow-path handlers. A network client can negotiate TLS-only RDP and send Fast-Path input before Confirm Active or valid credentials, injecting synthetic input into the host user’s X11 session. The advisory reports no screen/content disclosure or denial of service.
ai_role: The primary FreeRDP advisory states that Claude was used to analyze source code, build the reproduction harness and draft the report. The reporter says the protocol-level reproduction was executed against an unmodified FreeRDP shadow server and independently verified. The exact Claude model/version is not identified.
classification_note: The FreeRDP advisory was published on 2026-11-09. No cited source reports exploitation in the wild or establishes zero-day status.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies FreeRDP 3.33.0 as patched. It also explains that the earlier 3.32.0 change fixed slow-path handlers only and left the Fast-Path handlers unguarded; exact merged remediation commit is not linked in the advisory. This does not establish patch deployment.

impacts.conditions: A network client can reach a FreeRDP shadow server and send Fast-Path input before completing Confirm Active or providing credentials. The demonstrated target is the host user’s X11 session; the advisory does not demonstrate disclosure of screen contents or a crash/denial of service.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a reproducible controlled test against an unmodified build; it does not report exploitation in the wild.
